1970年代初，The Moody Blues鼓手Graeme Edge與Sus: In the early 1970s the Moody Blues drummer Graeme Edge worked with Brian Groves, a professor at the University of Sussex, to create an electronic drum, used in 1971 on the song Procession. In 1976 Pollard Industries brought out the first commercial electronic drum, the Syndrum, but the business failed. Simmons was founded in 1978, and in 1981 the SDSV with its hexagonal pads entered pop and rock line-ups. In the 1980s Pearl, Roland and Yamaha joined in; in 1997 the Roland TD-10 moved to mathematical modelling and mesh pads, which later became V-Drums. After the 2000s digital sound sources became common, and in the 2010s high-end models improved triggering, cymbals and hi-hat response.

演奏者將鼓墊與鈸片依類原聲鼓組配置架設，手持鼓棒敲擊鼓墊；每次敲擊由感測器產生訊: The player sets up the pads and cymbal pads in the layout of an acoustic kit and strikes the pads with sticks; each strike makes a sensor produce a signal, which travels by cable to the drum module and comes out as the matching drum or cymbal sound. Beginners can practise on headphones, or through a PA system or a mixer. A kit with a digital music interface can also trigger other digital music interface sounds.

電子鼓可接鍵盤擴大機或公共廣播系統用於現場樂團演出，也可接耳機作無聲練習，或接音: Electronic drums can go through a keyboard amp or a PA system for live band work, through headphones for silent practice, or into an audio mixer for recording; a kit with a musical instrument digital interface can also trigger any of its sounds. The early device was made by Graeme Edge with Brian Groves and was used on the 1971 song Procession; commercial electronic drums were used by Richard James Burgess on Chant No. 1 and Angel Face, and appeared in 1980s pop and rock, synth-pop and progressive rock line-ups.
電子鼓的演奏墊多為圓盤或淺殼，表面常覆橡膠、矽膠或布狀塗層，以提供鼓棒回彈；部分: The pads of an electronic drum are mostly discs or shallow shells, often covered with rubber, silicone or a cloth-like surface to give the stick its rebound; the cymbals of some kits are plastic or special acoustic/electronic cymbals. Piezo sensors are embedded in the silicone, the rubber pad or the cymbal, or mounted under the drumhead. In 1997 the Roland TD-10 moved to mesh pads made of two layers of tightly stretched woven mesh fibre. The materials of the shells, stands and sound module are not stated in the source.
電子鼓的音色由音源模組產生，可合成或取樣鼓、鈸與世界／管弦打擊樂器；若具MIDI: The sound of an electronic drum is produced by the sound module, which can synthesise or sample drums, cymbals and world or orchestral percussion; with MIDI (musical instrument digital interface) it can also trigger other electronic sounds. It does not sound through a vibrating drumhead: a piezo sensor detects the force and position of the strike and the module outputs the result, so the volume can be set through headphones, a keyboard amplifier, a PA system or an audio mixer. High-end modules offer tuning, head type, material and effects, the head and the rim can give different sounds, the hi-hat can sense opening and closing and foot pressure, and the cymbal is divided into edge, bow, bell and choked. The range depends on the chosen sound and settings.
電子鼓（Electronic Drums）屬21膜鳴鼓類，是模擬鼓組或其他打擊樂: Electronic drums belong to class 21, membranophones, and are electronic instruments that imitate the sound and look of a drum kit or other percussion. They consist of a sound module that generates synthesised or sampled percussion sounds and pads fitted with electronic sensors; the pads are mostly struck with sticks, and the signal goes back along a cable to the module, which makes the sound. The way of playing is close to an acoustic kit, though the feel differs a little. Drummers and percussionists can use them in live bands, for silent practice on headphones, or for recording.
